uncited: This family builds on [Multi-Pass and Compositing Techniques](14748-multi-pass-and-compositing-techniques.md) and is distinct from [Projection and MIP Techniques](6305-projection-and-mip-techniques.md) because it explicitly tracks opacity and transmittance for alpha blending, preserving depth cues, whereas MIP methods discard opacity for order-independent extremum aggregation.

It differs from [Volume Raycasting Output Generation](4277-volume-raycasting-output-generation.md) by focusing on the mathematical accumulation logic itself, while the sibling article covers the broader implementation pipeline including ray traversal and transfer function sampling.
